requirements.evidence: Covers every endpoint and the contract: pairing with \A\d{6}\z format check -> 400 (app/Http/Controllers/Totem/AuthController.php:23-28), one 401 for unknown/expired/consumed/inactive codes under lockForUpdate in a transaction (app/Actions/PairTotem.php:129-151), totems row + JWT with totem_id/entity_id/preset_id/queues/iat/exp/jti (app/Totem/TotemToken.php:911-923 hunk), response includes entity slug/name. Middleware re-checks totem/preset activity and entity match, then intersects claims with the current join (app/Http/Middleware/AuthenticateTotem.php:645-670). TotemContext::queue gives 404 for unknown or foreign slugs and 403 when out of scope. Ticket goes through IssueTicket with TicketChannel::Totem (TicketController.php:586). 429 rate_limited rendering, CORS pattern and preflight, throttles 10/30, .env.example, phpunit.xml, and doc updates are all present. The gap: composer.json adds firebase/php-jwt ^7.2 but no composer.lock change is in the diff, so a locked install would not pull in the library.

conventions.evidence: Domain writes go through new Actions (app/Actions/PairTotem.php, OpenTotemPairingWindow.php), and issuance reuses IssueTicket. Migrations have reversible down() and timestamped generator-style names. Models set #[Fillable] deliberately and keep login_code_* system-set via forceFill. PHPDoc is on public methods. CHANGELOG, docs/api/totem.md, database-schema.md, architecture.md and ops docs are updated. Small deviations: input checks are hand-rolled instead of $request->validate (justified by the custom error codes), and the change adds new App\Totem / App\Context helper namespaces (TotemToken, PairedTotem).

security.evidence: No oracle on pairing: one InvalidPairingCodeException maps to 401 invalid_pairing_code, and the reason only goes to the audit log, never the code (PairTotem.php:144-150). Codes come from random_int and are zero-padded. The HS256 secret must be at least 32 chars (TotemToken::secret). Claims are type-checked (AuthenticateTotem.php:645-648). Totem, preset and entity are re-validated on every call. Queues are resolved only within the token entity (TotemContext.php:280). The priority must be an int enum value. CORS sets no credentials, uses an anchored origin regex, and only the needed headers. The rate-limit key hashes the bearer token, so the raw JWT is never a cache key.

tests.evidence: Seven Pest files cover the following. Pairing: success claims, format dataset, the four 401 cases, reuse, regeneration, 429 and audit-without-code. CORS: preflight 204, a foreign origin, TOTEM_WEB_ORIGIN, and the Authorization header. Command: zero padding, replacement, and the unknown-preset failure exit. Middleware: missing, malformed, wrong-secret, expired, TTL, malformed-claims, deleted/deactivated totem and preset, entity mismatch, soft-deleted entity, last_seen_at. Listings: ordering, scope intersection, 403/404/422. Issuance: sequential codes, each priority, invalid/missing/float priority creating nothing, inactive queue, foreign slugs, 30/min throttle.

simplicity.evidence: Uses a well-known library (firebase/php-jwt), reuses IssueTicket and InactiveQueueException, and keeps priorities in one source of truth (app/Enums/TotemPriority.php) for both listing and validation. Controllers are thin invokables. There is some extra indirection: PairedTotem DTO, TotemContext container binding and a TotemApiException carrying headers. It is reasonable but slightly more structure than strictly required.

readability.evidence: Classes are small and well named, with comments explaining non-obvious choices ('\\A...\\z rather than ^...$', the rate-limit keying rationale in AppServiceProvider, the php-jwt real clock note in TotemToken). There is no dead code or debug output, and the style matches siblings (casts(), #[Fillable], PHPDoc generics).

scope.evidence: Nearly everything serves the task. Env plumbing in bin/pf and docker/compose.vps.yml is deployment support for the new secret, and the docs/ops updates track it. OpenTotemPairingWindow also refuses inactive presets (OpenTotemPairingWindow.php:62-64), which the task did not ask for, though it is documented and tested. Appearance-driven queue visuals (TotemPreset::queueVisual) go slightly beyond the minimum contract but fill required fields.

issues.explanation: firebase/php-jwt ^7.2 is added to composer.json but composer.lock is not in the diff, so `composer install` from the lock file would not install the library and every totem endpoint would fail with a missing class.
The command refuses to open a pairing window for an inactive preset, a rule the task did not specify (pairing already rejects inactive presets at /api/totem/auth).

Tokens are issued with Carbon's clock but verified with php-jwt's real clock, so tests that travel forward before pairing would hit an iat-in-the-future rejection; the comment documents this, but it is a subtle test trap.
Input checks for code/priority are hand-rolled instead of $request->validate; this is justified by the custom error-code bodies but departs from the stated controller validation pattern.
The ticket throttle is keyed by a hash of the bearer token rather than the totem id, so re-pairing the same device gets a fresh 30/min budget.

review.summary: The change implements the full totem BFF. It adds three migrations and the models and factories, the pairing command and Action, a locked-transaction pairing endpoint with HS256 JWT, a totem.auth middleware that intersects the token scope with the current preset join, the queues, priorities and ticket endpoints (ticket via IssueTicket), JSON 429/error rendering, CORS, and thorough docs and tests. Security and test coverage are strong. The main defect is a missing composer.lock update for the new firebase/php-jwt dependency, plus a few small scope and convention nits, so I would approve once the lock file is committed.
